pr_title: tmpfiles: resolve specifiers from the target root
pr_body:
the --root option is supposed to set up an isolated,
dormant system.
For that its necessary to inspect the target root for
information that is necessary for machine-id, hostname
and similar specifiers.

Some open points are what should happen with `--root=/` and what if `--user` is specified as well (should that even be possible?)

Fixes: #16183

Ok, clened up formatting, adding a description to `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md` and added a check to disallow `--root` and `--user` at the same time.

For me this is sufficient, I might add some more ENV variables to override Hostname ad a later time.

If the specifier_printf() issue is all that's left, I would be more than happy to submit those changes!

Please do. There's no guarantee that other things will not pop up in further review, this is open source after all, but at the moment it seems that this series is almost ready.

> ping?

I'll try to work on the last remaining issues this week. The last few weeks have been crazy busy! Sorry about that!

In case the ping was at me, I wont touch this for a while.

Primary reason because I believe shoehorning this into `userdata` will mean that this will be part of the interface and would need some extensibility. You then cant use specifier that expects something else than a rootfs prefix in `userdata`, at least at the same time.
So there would need to be some extensible struct passed in.

I tried to keep the changes local to the `tmpfiles` tool, not re-think the "specifiers" framework.

No need to. The "userdata" pointer is not used in tmpfiles at all so far, all calls to specifier_printf() in tmpfiles just pass it as NULL right now. The parameter exists only for cases like this, use it! 

You shouldn't need to touch the generic specifier handling code at all, all changes can remain local to tmpfiles.d. All that needs to be done is replace some specifier handler functions listed in the `specifier_table[]` and passing the prefix in the so far unused userdata argument.

If I change, say `specifier_os_version_id` so that it will interpret `userdata` as prefix, then funky things will happen if
it is used elsewhere, with say a `Unit *` 
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/427103f7a627af9a89b5eb470b13c8ff50ca43ae/src/core/unit-printf.c#L227

> 
> You shouldn't need to touch the generic specifier handling code at all, all changes can remain local to tmpfiles.d. All that needs to be done is replace some specifier handler functions listed in the `specifier_table[]` and passing the prefix in the so far unused userdata argument.

I cant change  the specifier callbacks to use the userdata. Or do you imply that I wrap every specifier callback?

I would expect that a separate table is alot less hassle, and one thats not `const` could be patched if one wants to add further overrides in the future.

I posted PR #20017 now. It's an attempt to solve this thoroughly across the tree, i.e. also in sysusers, repart, systemctl. It doesn't do the blocking of the resolution of the runtime specifiers, because it's not clear to me this is good and necessary.

Let's close this one and continue there.

issue_context.title: systemd-tmpfiles will resolve specifiers (machine-id, etc) from host, not from target --root
issue_context.body:
This is a follow-up to #14806, systemd-tmpfiles learned to use {passwd,group} databases from the root systemd, but will still use the host /etc/machine-id, /etc/os-release and so on.

Ideally it will pick such configuration files only from the target rootfs, while not handling entries containing non-resolvable specifiers (boot, user id, etc..).
Any entry with questionable specifiers should be rather leftout than containing information from the running host.

the architecture could probably be added per environment or switch.

Did not know I'd do a PR shortly, kids stayed at a friends yesterday ;)

review_comments: the cast is not necessary still. as mentioned above "const void*" casts implicitly to "const char*" and the other way too!

instead of patching around in the specifier table, make them constant please, but have two around, one for the no-runtime case and one for the normal case. Yes, they will be mostly idnetical, but that's fine.
I can't make them constant, unless I use some static array for `prefix`. Otherwise the pointer to prefix will only be known at runtime
specifier_printf() has a third param, `userdata`, we only pass `NULL` there so far. Pass the `prefix` there instead.
hmm, split this bit into its own commit pls
